newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly down after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly down after recent gains.

text.p: After posting five record closes in a row, Swiss shares ended marginally lower on Tuesday in what was described as a welcome consolidation.
One dealer said sentiment continued to be favourable due to sound fundamentals such as the dollar's strength and a positive interest rate outlook.
"This correction seems like a perfect opportunity to jump on the bandwagon," one trader noted. He said the market expected further gains even though the recent increases had been dizzying.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended lower by 6.9 points or 0.13 percent at 5,361.9 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 1.86 points or 0.05 percent to 3,391.34.

Bourse volume stood at 2.48 billion Swiss francs. Trade was dominated by professionals, dealers said. Shares of technology company Sulzer were among the most prominent winners, while CS Group and SGS showed sizeable losses.

Sulzer jumped 77 francs, or 6.4 francs, to end at the all-time high of 1,280. Traders said speculation about forthcoming conditions for the planned flotation of the company's Sulzer Medica unit helped the stock.
Sulzer AG said it would publish detailed IPO conditions by early July.
Selling in CS Group continued amid some disappointment that various merger and spin-off rumours proved unfounded, dealers said. The stock eased 3.5 francs to 191.5.
Shares of inspection and controlling systems maker Surveillance slumped 130 francs, or more than four percent, to 3,080 francs.
One trader said this could stem from the fact that tax authorities have appealed a court decision supporting the company's view on share buyback plans.
Most-active Novartis registereds were up four francs to 2,047 on buying by Geneva-based banks, dealers said.
UBS bearers were up four francs at 1,687.
Nestle, which will be traded ex dividend of 30 francs on Wednesday, were up five francs to 1,855.
